subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should plugin-runtime callers be categorically denied patch access to legacy ownerless session rows, or should OpenClaw provide a trusted migration or operator-adoption path?
rationale: The PR changes authority over persisted legacy state; the sibling delete rule supports fail-closed isolation, but the permanent upgrade contract requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Fail closed
options.body: Reject ownerless rows and document or test the operator-facing upgrade outcome.

options.title: Migrate ownership
options.body: Add a trusted doctor or operator migration before plugin mutation is allowed.

options.title: Defer legacy restriction
options.body: Land explicitly foreign-owned-row rejection now and decide ownerless authority separately.

recommendation.title: Fail closed
recommendation.body: Reject ownerless rows and document or test the operator-facing upgrade outcome.

likelyOwner.reason: His feature history owns the projection and storage boundary where this authority contract is enforced.
